answer: An agent economy can resist sybils like a tended garden: every agent stakes a small deposit before joining, and the stake is slashed when peers prove a fake identity. Each agent also carries a unique pigment — a reputation built from attested work history — so clones start colorless and cannot inherit trust. A cipher-bound proof links each action to one identity, making mass sockpuppets expensive to maintain and easy to spot when their histories do not match.
